_note: Canned interview answers for a made-up person, so the project demonstrates itself on first run. Replace with your own, or run init.py with no flags and answer out loud.

profile.name: Mira
profile.work: Product designer at a 40-person logistics startup, and I post about design on the side.
facts: Designer for 9 years, the last 4 in logistics software
Deaf in the left ear, so I prefer written over calls
Runs on a 2021 MacBook Air, no second monitor
units: Metric only. Never convert to imperial.

work.role: Product designer owning the dispatcher-facing side of a logistics platform.
focus: Redesign of the dispatch board, in build, ships end of Q2
Cutting the driver onboarding flow from 11 screens to 5
Writing the first version of our design system docs
projects: Dispatch board v3: design done, engineering 60% through, I review builds Tuesdays
Driver onboarding: research done, 3 concepts, no decision yet
Design system docs: 4 of 22 components written
constraints: No new engineering headcount until July
I work 09:00 to 15:30, school pickup is hard-stop
Dispatchers use the product 8 hours a day on 1366x768 screens
Anything touching driver pay needs legal review first
people: Tomas, my PM, decides scope, prefers one recommendation not three options
Ines, engineering lead on dispatch, will say yes to anything then run out of time
Hugo, head of ops, the actual customer, never reads documents longer than a page
vocabulary: Board = the dispatch board, the main screen, not a kanban
Leg = one pickup-to-dropoff segment of a shipment
Exception = a shipment that needs human attention right now
Tendering = offering a load to a carrier
help: Write like Hugo is reading it: one page, plain words, no design jargon
Give me one recommendation with the reasoning, not a menu
Assume dispatchers are experts and in a hurry, never explain the basics to them
If something needs legal review, say so before I get attached to it

channels: Instagram, 2 carousels a week, design teardowns
A newsletter, every other Thursday, about 700 words
LinkedIn, reposts of the carousels, low effort on purpose
audience: Designers 2 to 6 years in, mostly outside the US
They want to get better at arguing for their work, not at Figma
They skim on a phone, standing up
voice: Short sentences. One idea per line.
Always a concrete example before the principle
Numbers instead of adjectives: 11 screens to 5, not 'much simpler'
First person, lowercase headlines, no exclamation marks
pipeline: Idea goes in a note on my phone during the week
Sunday: pick one, write the newsletter first
Carousel is cut down from the newsletter, never the reverse
Draft sits overnight before it goes out
banned: The words unlock, elevate, game-changer, delve
Threads of 12 posts where 3 would do
Captions that just repeat the slides
help: Cut, do not add. If a draft can be shorter, shorten it.
Flag any line that would apply to any designer anywhere
Keep my phrasing, do not rewrite me into a brand voice

household: Me, my partner Dani, two kids, a flat in Alvalade
No car, everything is walking or metro
people: Dani, partner, nurse, rotating shifts including some nights
Nora, 6, started school this year, still naps at weekends
rhythms: School run 08:15, pickup 15:45, both on me unless Dani is off
Dani works two weekends a month
Friday evenings are nothing-planned by rule
Grandparents visit the first weekend of each month
care: Nora's school is going badly, I do not want cheerful advice about it
My mother's health, mention only if I bring it up
help: Planning help should respect the 15:45 hard stop without being reminded
Suggest things reachable without a car
Short answers. I am usually typing this one-handed.

setup: Salary 3,400 EUR net monthly, paid on the 24th
Newsletter sponsorships, 200 to 600 EUR a month, irregular
Dani and I split fixed costs from a joint account, everything else separate
I do my own tax as a sole trader for the content income
goals: Six months of fixed costs in cash: 9,400 of 14,000 EUR saved
No debt except 640 EUR a month on the flat until 2039
Want the content income to cover a four-day week by 2028
rules: Nothing bought the same day I first want it
Sponsorship money goes straight to savings, it is not salary
I keep a 1,000 EUR buffer and do not count it as savings
care: No investing advice. I have decided what I am doing.
Do not suggest cutting the kids' activities.
help: Do the arithmetic and show it, I will decide
If a plan assumes steady sponsorship income, say so out loud
